title: Learning Beyond the Classroom
text:
Many families now support their children's learning at home, especially when they are preparing for important tests. However, parents often worry that grades alone do not show how much a student really understands. Teachers therefore recommend combining regular quizzes with projects, which reveal progress over time. As a result, students who practise little and often tend to perform better than those who only study before exams.

Home learning works best when it is organised around clear goals rather than constant pressure. A short daily routine, such as reading for twenty minutes or reviewing one topic, can be more effective than long sessions on weekends. Moreover, children should be encouraged to explain what they have learned in their own words. This habit helps them identify gaps in their understanding before a test reveals them.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do teachers recommend combining with regular quizzes?
options: Projects that show progress over time

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what can be more effective than long sessions on weekends?
What can be inferred about students who only study before exams?
options: They are likely to retain less than students who study regularly
They always get the best grades
They do not need feedback from teachers

questions.text: Why does the author suggest asking children to explain what they have learned?
options: To reduce the number of tests they take
To discover gaps in their understanding before a test does

paragraph_translations: Muchas familias apoyan ahora el aprendizaje de sus hijos en casa, sobre todo cuando se preparan para exámenes importantes. Sin embargo, los padres a menudo temen que las calificaciones por sí solas no muestren cuánto entiende realmente un estudiante. Por ello, los profesores recomiendan combinar las pruebas cortas periódicas con proyectos, que revelan el progreso a lo largo del tiempo. Como resultado, los estudiantes que practican poco pero con frecuencia tienden a rendir mejor que quienes solo estudian antes de los exámenes.

El aprendizaje en casa funciona mejor cuando está organizado en torno a objetivos claros y no bajo presión constante. Una rutina diaria breve, como leer durante veinte minutos o repasar un tema, puede ser más eficaz que largas sesiones los fines de semana. Además, se debe animar a los niños a explicar lo que han aprendido con sus propias palabras. Este hábito les ayuda a identificar lagunas en su comprensión antes de que un examen las revele.
